mission.title: kubernetes: Rollback Deployment with kubectl rollout undo after bad image causes ImagePullBackOff
mission.description: After `kubectl set image` to a nonexistent tag, new pods show `ImagePullBackOff` / `ErrImagePull` (`manifest for web:v2.0.9 not found`) and the rollout stalls. Rollback with `kubectl rollout undo` restores the previous ReplicaSet.

steps.title: Identify the stalled rollout
steps.description:
```bash
kubectl rollout status deploy/web -n shop --timeout=60s
kubectl get pods -n shop -l app=web
kubectl describe pod -n shop -l app=web | grep -A3 -i 'Failed to pull'
```

steps.title: Review revision history
steps.description:
```bash
kubectl rollout history deploy/web -n shop
kubectl rollout history deploy/web -n shop --revision=2
```

Confirm the previous revision uses a working image.

steps.title: Undo the rollout
steps.description:
```bash
kubectl rollout undo deploy/web -n shop
# or a specific revision
kubectl rollout undo deploy/web -n shop --to-revision=2
```

steps.title: Verify recovery
steps.description:
```bash
kubectl rollout status deploy/web -n shop
kubectl get deploy web -n shop -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
```

steps.title: Fix the manifest to prevent re-applying the bad tag
steps.description:
```bash
grep -rn 'image:' k8s/web-deployment.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/web-deployment.yaml
```

Also set `spec.revisionHistoryLimit: 10` so undo targets remain available.

resolution.summary: The root cause is that the Deployment's pod template referenced an image tag that does not exist in the registry, so the new ReplicaSet's pods can never pull and the rollout stalls. `rollout undo` restores the previous pod template from the retained ReplicaSet, because old ReplicaSets keep their specs; healthy pods from it were never removed thanks to maxUnavailable.

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with kubernetes available or the issue environment reproducible.
